q: The motion of an object in both the x and y directions simultaneously is called _____ motion.
e: Two-dimensional motion occurs when an object moves in a plane, involving both x and y directions.

q: In two-dimensional motion, the displacement vector from point P to Q is denoted as _____ .
e: The textbook uses $\Delta \vec{r}$ to represent the displacement vector between two points in a plane.

q: The magnitude of the displacement vector $\Delta \vec{r}$ is given by _____ .
e: The magnitude is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem on the perpendicular components.

q: The direction of the displacement vector $\Delta \vec{r}$ is found using _____ .
e: The tangent of the angle is the ratio of vertical to horizontal displacement components.

q: An object moving with constant speed along a curved path is accelerating because _____ .
e: Even with constant speed, changing direction means velocity (a vector) changes, so acceleration occurs.

q: The direction of the velocity of an object moving along a curved path is always _____ to its path.
e: Velocity is tangential to the path at every point in curved motion.
This is the textbook's definition of instantaneous velocity as the limit of average velocity.
Average acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time interval.
It is the limit of average acceleration as the time interval approaches zero.

q: An object is accelerated whenever the velocity changes in _____ .
e: Acceleration occurs if either or both the magnitude and direction of velocity change.
